# Resource: stripe_refund

A refund of a payment intent or a charge. Set one of `payment_intent` and `charge`; Stripe fills in the other when the charge belongs to a payment intent, and fills in `customer` with the payment intent's customer. Without `amount`, it refunds what remains of the payment. Only `metadata` changes after creation.

~> A refund can move real money. In a live-mode Stripe account, creating or changing one fails at plan time unless the provider sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. Reading or importing one never does. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode. See the Managing Test Data guide.

~> Stripe cannot delete or undo a refund. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the refund, fail at plan time. To stop managing a refund, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_payment_intent" "order" {
  amount         = 2000
  currency       = "usd"
  payment_method = "pm_card_visa"
  status         = "succeeded"

  automatic_payment_methods = {
    enabled         = true
    allow_redirects = "never"
  }
}

# Refund part of the payment. Without `amount`, the refund is for what remains.
resource "stripe_refund" "partial" {
  payment_intent = stripe_payment_intent.order.id
  amount         = 500
  reason         = "requested_by_customer"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are optional:

* `amount` - (Optional) Amount, in cents (or local equivalent). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `charge` - (Optional) The identifier of the charge to refund. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `currency` - (Optional) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `customer` - (Optional) Customer whose customer balance to refund from. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `instructions_email` - (Optional) For payment methods without native refund support (e.g., Konbini, PromptPay), use this email from the customer to receive refund instructions. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `origin` - (Optional) Origin of the refund Possible values: `customer_balance`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `payment_intent` - (Optional) The identifier of the PaymentIntent to refund. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `reason` - (Optional) String indicating the reason for the refund. If set, possible values are `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, and `requested_by_customer`. If you believe the charge to be fraudulent, specifying `fraudulent` as the reason will add the associated card and email to your [block lists](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/lists), and will also help us improve our fraud detection algorithms. Possible values: `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `requested_by_customer`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `refund_application_fee` - (Optional) Boolean indicating whether the application fee should be refunded when refunding this charge. If a full charge refund is given, the full application fee will be refunded. Otherwise, the application fee will be refunded in an amount proportional to the amount of the charge refunded. An application fee can be refunded only by the application that created the charge. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `reverse_transfer` - (Optional) Boolean indicating whether the transfer should be reversed when refunding this charge. The transfer will be reversed proportionally to the amount being refunded (either the entire or partial amount).<br><br>A transfer can be reversed only by the application that created the charge. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `balance_transaction` - Balance transaction that describes the impact on your account balance.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `customer_account` - ID of the account of this refund.
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. You can use this for displaying to users (available on non-card refunds only).
* `destination_details` - See [`destination_details`](#destination_details) below.
* `failure_balance_transaction` - After the refund fails, this balance transaction describes the adjustment made on your account balance that reverses the initial balance transaction.
* `failure_reason` - Provides the reason for the refund failure. Possible values are: `lost_or_stolen_card`, `expired_or_canceled_card`, `charge_for_pending_refund_disputed`, `insufficient_funds`, `declined`, `merchant_request`, or `unknown`.
* `next_action` - See [`next_action`](#next_action) below.
* `payment_method` - ID of the payment method associated with this refund.
* `pending_reason` - Provides the reason for why the refund is pending. Possible values are: `processing`, `insufficient_funds`, or `charge_pending`. Possible values: `charge_pending`, `insufficient_funds`, `processing`.
* `presentment_details` - See [`presentment_details`](#presentment_details) below.
* `receipt_number` - This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this refund.
* `source_transfer_reversal` - The transfer reversal that's associated with the refund. Only present if the charge came from another Stripe account.
* `status` - Status of the refund. This can be `pending`, `requires_action`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `canceled`. Learn more about [failed refunds](https://docs.stripe.com/refunds#failed-refunds).
* `transfer_reversal` - This refers to the transfer reversal object if the accompanying transfer reverses. This is only applicable if the charge was created using the destination parameter.

* `jp_bank_transfer` - See [`destination_details.jp_bank_transfer`](#destination_details.jp_bank_transfer) below.
* `mb_way` - See [`destination_details.mb_way`](#destination_details.mb_way) below.
* `multibanco` - See [`destination_details.multibanco`](#destination_details.multibanco) below.
* `mx_bank_transfer` - See [`destination_details.mx_bank_transfer`](#destination_details.mx_bank_transfer) below.
* `p24` - See [`destination_details.p24`](#destination_details.p24) below.
* `paypal` - See [`destination_details.paypal`](#destination_details.paypal) below.
* `swish` - See [`destination_details.swish`](#destination_details.swish) below.
* `th_bank_transfer` - See [`destination_details.th_bank_transfer`](#destination_details.th_bank_transfer) below.
* `type` - The type of transaction-specific details of the payment method used in the refund (e.g., `card`). An additional hash is included on `destination_details` with a name matching this value. It contains information specific to the refund transaction.
* `us_bank_transfer` - See [`destination_details.us_bank_transfer`](#destination_details.us_bank_transfer) below.

<a id="destination_details.blik"></a>
### `destination_details.blik`

The `destination_details.blik` attribute supports:

* `network_decline_code` - For refunds declined by the network, a decline code provided by the network which indicates the reason the refund failed.
* `reference` - The reference assigned to the refund.
* `reference_status` - Status of the reference on the refund. This can be `pending`, `available` or `unavailable`.

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a refund whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_refund.partial

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_refund.partial
```

The refund stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a refund using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_refund.partial
  id = "re_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_refund.partial
  identity = {
    id = "re_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the refund.

Using `terraform import`, import a refund using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_refund.partial re_123
```

-> Stripe does not return `origin`, `refund_application_fee` or `reverse_transfer`, so an imported refund has them null.
